description: A college team passionate about space technology, innovation, science, and solving real-world problems through technology.
summary:
Wildfire monitoring relies heavily on satellite data from instruments like MODIS and VIIRS, but differing resolutions—1 km versus 375 m—and inherent sensor biases create significant discrepancies in historical fire records.

To solve this, we developed ARKAGNI, an end-to-end data harmonization engine designed to reconcile active-fire observations across different satellite platforms. ARKAGNI processes raw hotspot data through a rigorous pipeline featuring local DuckDB/Parquet storage, leakage-free diurnal fitting, and automated manifest integrity verification.

By bridging the resolution and calibration gap between MODIS and VIIRS, ARKAGNI provides researchers and emergency responders with a unified, continuous, and reliable fire-monitoring dataset. This ensures that long-term climate analyses and wildfire tracking remain accurate, consistent, and independent of individual sensor transitions.
details:
What it does & how it works: ARKAGNI is a data processing tool built with a FastAPI backend and a React frontend. It takes active-fire data from MODIS and VIIRS satellites, stores it locally using DuckDB and Parquet, and aligns the differing resolutions (1 km vs. 375 m) to make historical fire records easier to compare.

Benefits & impact: It bridges the gap between older MODIS data and newer, higher-resolution VIIRS observations, giving researchers a more consistent dataset for tracking and analyzing wildfires over time.

Tools & technologies used: Python, FastAPI, React, DuckDB, Parquet, and Docker.

Design approach: Built on a high-performance local data architecture using DuckDB and Parquet, ensuring instant query execution, complete offline reliability, and a seamless setup for anyone running the project.
